This follows an initial announcement of the technology in May 2024. TPUs are Google's custom-developed AI accelerator chips designed for high-performance machine learning workloads. Trillium, which was used to train Google's Gemini 2.0 AI model, is a key component of the company's AI Hypercomputer architecture. Compared to its predecessor (TPU v5e), Trillium delivers a 4.7x increase in peak compute performance per chip and is over 67% more energy-efficient. It also features double the High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) capacity and bandwidth. The general availability of Trillium was accompanied by enhancements to the AI Hypercomputer's software layer, including optimizations for frameworks like JAX, PyTorch, and TensorFlow. <3> Google initiated the rollout of its third core update for 2024 on November 11, 2024. The update's stated goal was to enhance search result quality by prioritizing content that is genuinely useful to users over content designed primarily for search engine performance. While initially anticipated to take about two weeks, the rollout was officially completed on December 5, 2024, lasting approximately 24 days. Google confirmed the completion through its Search Central social media channels and the Search Status Dashboard. <4> On October 29, 2024, Alphabet announced its financial results for the third quarter of 2024, reporting a 15% year-over-year increase in revenue to $88.25 billion, up from $76.7 billion in the same period of the previous year. The strong performance was driven by significant growth in the company's advertising business. Additionally, Google Cloud's revenue surged to $11.3 billion, a year-over-year increase of $2.9 billion, with CEO Sundar Pichai attributing the momentum to AI offerings that are attracting new customers and larger deals. <5> On October 28, 2024, Google announced its largest global expansion of AI Overviews in Search, making the feature available in over 100 countries and territories. [1, 2, 4] The Pixel Tablet received new screensaver options, including a home panel to control smart home devices and the ability to cast media to nearby Pixel phones. [1, 3] All Pixel Watch models gained a new Individual Contact Tile for quick access to a favorite contact and the ability to add emoji reactions in Gmail. This funding is for the first year of a project that could last three years. The initiative, known as Systems Biology Data Platform (SysBio) Leveraging the Accelerating Medicines Partnership, will focus on creating a centralized portal called SysBio FAIRplex. This platform will enable researchers to analyze complex, multi-modal data from over ten diseases across existing Accelerating Medicines Partnership® (AMP®) programs to better understand disease mechanisms. <9> In the antitrust lawsuit initiated by Epic Games, a U.S. District Court judge issued a three-year permanent injunction against Google on October 7, 2024. This injunction mandates that Google open its Play Store by allowing the distribution of alternative app stores through Google Play and granting them access to its app catalog. The ruling also requires Google to permit users to download apps from these competing stores and allows developers to inform users about payment systems outside of Google's. Furthermore, the injunction blocks Google from entering into exclusive distribution agreements or offering monetary benefits to developers for Play Store exclusivity. Following the ruling, on October 18, 2024, the same judge granted Google a partial administrative stay, temporarily pausing some of these requirements while the appeals process continues.

This decision was primarily driven by the strong momentum and performance of Google Cloud, which demonstrated significant revenue and margin growth in Alphabet's third quarter. The analyst update followed Alphabet's Q3 earnings report, which revealed a 16% year-over-year revenue increase to $102.3 billion. <5> Morningstar increased its fair value estimate for Alphabet (GOOGL) to $340 per share from $300, following the company's third-quarter results which exceeded expectations. The primary driver for this valuation increase was the significant 79% growth in Google Cloud's backlog. This growth prompted Morningstar to revise its five-year growth forecast for Google Cloud to 34%, up from a previous forecast of 30%. The firm also noted potential future upside from the monetization of artificial intelligence through Google Cloud and the continued solid performance of its search business. <6> During Alphabet's Q3 2025 earnings call on October 29, 2025, CEO Sundar Pichai announced that Waymo is expanding its autonomous vehicle operations to three new U.S. cities: Dallas, Denver, and Seattle. This move is part of an accelerated commercial expansion phase for the company. While not part of the earnings call announcement, Waymo has also revealed longer-term plans to launch in Nashville. The company is already testing vehicles in Dallas and has stated plans to launch in Denver in the fall. <7> Google has launched a public beta for Pomelli, a new AI-powered marketing tool from Google Labs and Google DeepMind, with the announcement and launch occurring on October 28, 2025. This tool is designed to assist small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) in creating on-brand promotional content. By analyzing a company's website, Pomelli identifies key brand elements like tone of voice, colors, fonts, and images to generate customized marketing materials, aiming to simplify campaign creation for businesses with limited resources. <8> Verily and NVIDIA announced a strategic collaboration on October 28, 2025, to accelerate the development of AI in precision health. This integration provides researchers on Verily's Workbench with access to the latest GPUs, such as the NVIDIA Blackwell and Hopper, significantly speeding up analyses like genomic data processing from hours to minutes. A key application of this collaboration will be to power the National Institutes of Health's (NIH) 'All of Us' Researcher Workbench, which supports a global community of nearly 20,000 researchers. Powered by Google's Gemini AI, the coach acts as a conversational assistant, creating personalized and adaptive plans for fitness, sleep, and general wellness. It can generate specific workouts based on user goals and available equipment, analyze sleep patterns to provide recommendations, and answer a range of health-related questions. The feature is integrated into a redesigned Fitbit app and is intended to become more widely available in the following year. <10> Verily, Alphabet's precision health subsidiary, launched its new consumer health application, "Verily Me," at the HLTH USA 2025 conference, which took place from October 19-22, 2025, in Las Vegas. The free application is designed to provide users with personalized health recommendations from licensed clinicians who review the patient's consolidated medical history from various providers. A key feature of the app is an AI companion named "Violet," which can securely answer users' questions about their medical records and general health.

The API supports background execution, enabling clients to trigger tasks asynchronously, disconnect, and poll for results later without hitting timeouts. <2> On December 11, 2025, Google Labs announced the introduction of 'Disco,' an experimental AI-powered web browser built on Chromium. Designed to shape the future of web browsing, Disco utilizes the Gemini 3 model and introduces a flagship feature known as 'GenTabs'. <3> On December 11, 2025, Google initiated a global core algorithm update affecting its search engine ranking results. <4> On December 5, 2025, U.S. District Judge Amit P. Mehta entered a Final Judgment in the DOJ's landmark antitrust case against Google Search. The 226-page remedies ruling imposed strict behavioral constraints, including a broad prohibitory injunction that bars Google from entering or maintaining exclusive distribution contracts related to Google Search, Chrome, Google Assistant, or the Gemini app. The court established a 'Google shall not condition' rule, which prevents the company from making access or favorable terms contingent on using other Google products or sidelining competitors, and mandated that any default agreements end after one year without automatic renewals. However, the ruling served as a blow to the DOJ and state attorneys general by rejecting requests for structural remedies; Google will not be forced to divest its Chrome web browser or its Android operating system, as the court found the plaintiffs overreached in their divestiture proposals. The decision aims to dismantle Google's unlawful exclusivity and restore competition without imposing product redesigns or forced breakups. <5> Google announced the launch of Gemini 3, a major update to its AI model and the Gemini app. The update detailed upgraded reasoning capabilities, "vibe coding", and a new experimental Gemini Agent. <6> On November 18, 2025, Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai warned against 'irrational exuberance' in the AI market and confirmed that the company's 2030 net-zero emissions targets will be delayed due to the substantial energy demands of artificial intelligence. <7> On November 14, 2025, Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai, alongside Texas Governor Greg Abbott, announced a $40 billion multi-year investment in Texas. Funded through 2027, the investment will be used to build three new AI data center campuses—two in Haskell County and one in Armstrong County—to support expanded cloud and computing capacity, ensuring robust infrastructure for future artificial intelligence advancements. <8> On November 12, 2025, Alphabet's self-driving subsidiary, Waymo, announced that it will begin offering driverless robotaxi rides on freeways across San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Phoenix, initially making the service available to early-access users. <9> Alphabet Inc. closed concurrent SEC-registered underwritten public offerings, which included $17.5 billion in U.S. dollar-denominated senior notes and €6.5 billion in euro-denominated senior notes. <10> On October 30, 2025, Stifel raised its price target for Alphabet (GOOGL) to $333 from $292, while maintaining a 'Buy' rating on the stock. This decision was primarily driven by the strong momentum and performance of Google Cloud, which demonstrated significant revenue and margin growth in Alphabet's third quarter. The analyst update followed Alphabet's Q3 earnings report, which revealed a 16% year-over-year revenue increase to $102.3 billion.
